title: MyLinden Help: Autopay and Paperless Credit on a Signed Patient Payment Plans Installment
content:
**Does paying by automatic debit lower the installment of a Patient Payment Plans agreement?**

The autopay credit on the signed installment is 3.00 when the plan's automatic debit method is ACH and the statements of the patient's Patient Financial Account are delivered paperless; 1.50 when the method is card or HSA/FSA card and statements are delivered paperless; and 0.00 in every other case.

**How is the credit applied?** The credit, in dollars, is subtracted from the monthly installment worked out for the agreement before any credit. The signed installment is never below the tier's minimum installment and is rounded half up to the cent.

**Which records decide it?** The automatic debit method recorded on the plan (ACH, card, HSA/FSA card or none) and the statement delivery recorded on the Patient Financial Account.

| Automatic debit method | Statements delivered paperless | Autopay credit |
|---|---|---|
| ACH | Yes | 3.00 |
| ACH | No | 0.00 |
| Card or HSA/FSA card | Yes | 1.50 |
| Card or HSA/FSA card | No | 0.00 |
| None | Either | 0.00 |

**An example (hypothetical).** An installment of 118.00 before credit, a plan paying by ACH, statements delivered paperless: 118.00 less 3.00 is 115.00. Had the tier's minimum installment been 116.00, the signed installment would be held at 116.00.
